criterionText: Multi-project isolation is proven: distinct project ids, repository roots, thread bindings and worker bindings, with deliberately mismatched bindings refused and no cross-project leakage of prompt, evidence, decision, session or repository facts

twoRealProjects.note: Not synthetic fixtures. Both are real projects with their own live-configured gatekeeper transports that have actually made real, paid, live OpenAI calls throughout this programme.

distinctProjectIdsRepoRootsThreadBinding.citation: Already covered by scenario 9 of the pre-existing test suite: mismatched bindings refused before anything is sent.

workerBindingsDeterministic.citation: projectos/agent/test/loopRunner.test.ts, SESSION_WORKER_MISMATCH test: a session bound to one workerId, resumed under a run resolving a DIFFERENT workerId, is refused with zero worker calls (`calls` equals `[]`) — the refusal happens strictly before any dispatch.

testA.command: from C:/dev/ProjectOS: `projectos run --execute --resume --session PROJECTOS-DEGRADED-WITNESS3A-6919c3b07d3e-caf12f2a` (a real witness3 session id, real worker binding witness-inert)
testA.result: REFUSED (NO_SUCH_SESSION), exit 1, no worker dispatched — witness3's session is completely invisible to ProjectOS's execution context

testB.command: from C:/dev/projectos-degraded-witness3: `projectos run --execute --resume --session PROJECTOS-AUTONOMOUS-GATEKEEPER-LOOP1A-6b2bd107f83d-79532a25` (a real ProjectOS session id, real worker binding claude-local)
testB.result: REFUSED (NO_SUCH_SESSION), exit 1, no worker dispatched — symmetric refusal in the reverse direction

workerBindingsLiveCrossProject.interpretation: Session records live under each project's own .projectops/execution/, so a session id minted in one project's repository root is not merely refused by an identity check — it does not exist to be found at all in the other's. Worker bindings cannot cross a repository-root boundary by construction.

noCrossProjectLeakageOfDecisionAndCost.evidence: grep of every GKREQ-* request id in each project's independent gatekeeper-ledger.json: ProjectOS holds 10 real request ids, witness3 holds 2 real request ids, `comm -12` intersection is empty. No request, decision, or cost entry from one project has ever appeared in the other's ledger.

noCrossProjectLeakageOfPromptEvidenceSes.note: Governed by checkThreadBinding and the repository-root identity checks proven throughout this programme (distinct providerThreadId per project, distinct canonicalRepositoryIdentity per project, refused on mismatch) — unaffected by anything in this session's work.

conclusion: C13 fully proven: distinct project ids/repo roots/thread bindings (pre-existing, deterministic), worker-binding mismatch refused with zero dispatch (pre-existing, deterministic), and — the one gap the matrix flagged as never live-exercised — worker bindings deliberately mismatched across two REAL, independently live-gatekeeper-configured projects, refused symmetrically in both directions, with zero ledger overlap confirmed.
